To: lindqvist-family-blog
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: DRAFT — So this happened. Fernhollow Photo is real!!

Quick update from the trenches, except the trenches are now technically my own business??

Fernhollow Photo LLC is official. Filed, website up, actual weddings on the calendar. I am going out on my own as a wedding photographer. Which is a very normal sentence to type and apparently a much harder sentence to look at after you type it.

I wanted to tell you all before Thanksgiving because I love you, and also because I would like to eat Ruthie’s turkey without having to make a surprise business announcement while somebody passes the gravy. I know this family. There would be questions. Someone would get out a pen. My rolls would get cold.

So! Here is the news, with some answers in advance.

Rosebud Lane closed at the end of October. Marisol told me on October 6, and after four years shooting for her, it was a lot to take in. That place has been a huge part of my life. Most of the wedding stories you’ve had to hear from me, including the lens-cap criminal in the tulle dress, happened because of that job.

I’m really grateful to Marisol. She basically taught me everything. There’s knowing how to use a camera, and then there’s being the person who can keep taking pictures when the schedule has disappeared and everybody needs something at once. I learned so much of that from watching her work. She trusted me with more and more over those four years, and somewhere along the way I became someone who could actually do this on her own.

She also sent six of her 2027 couples my way. That kind of trust means a lot. Marisol, if you read this, thank you. I will probably say it another forty times and make it awkward. Sorry in advance.

The studio closing made the timing real, but this isn’t an idea I came up with in a panic three weeks ago. I’ve been planning it in my head for two years. Thinking about what I’d call it, what kind of work I wanted to do, how I wanted to work with couples. Apparently I could think about all of that forever, but actually filing the paperwork required sitting in a car outside Fred Meyer on my lunch break.

That’s where I filed the LLC on October 22. Very glamorous. Very business owner of me. I cried a little in the car afterward, which I feel was a reasonable response to becoming legally responsible for something with a name.

And the name is Fernhollow.

Grandma, this part is for you.

It’s from the fern hollow trail behind your old place in Gresham. That’s where I took my first real pictures with your Pentax. I keep coming back to that when I think about how all of this started. Before wedding schedules and lens purchases and knowing how many spare batteries I could fit into one bag, there was me, your camera, and that trail.

I wanted a name that meant something to me, and that one did. So now it’s on my website and my paperwork and, briefly, a cake.

Sam made a cake that said FERNHOLOW.

One L short. Still legally a cake. We ate it anyway.

He has been very good about living with someone who can be excited about a website one minute and staring at an email like it might bite her the next. Also, Mom, yes, Sam is coming to Thanksgiving. There, two major family announcements handled in one post.

Now for the part Dad is already scrolling down to find:

DAD. I HAVE SORTED OUT HEALTH INSURANCE.

I picked a marketplace plan on November 5. It starts January 1. I know you ask because you love me. I love you too. Please consider this the health insurance portion of Thanksgiving completed, preferably before anyone has even taken the foil off the stuffing.

And I do have work booked. Fourteen weddings for 2027 already! Six came through Marisol’s referrals, and eight found me on my own. June is the busiest month so far, with four weddings, and there’s one at Wallowa Lake in September. My calendar is starting to look like a wedding season instead of a very ambitious wish.

For the bigger weddings, Jae will second shoot with me, paid per wedding. So I’m not planning to sprint between two places at once and hope nobody notices. My knees have already submitted their feedback on that approach.

The booking that made this feel especially real was Dahlia and Ken. June 12, at Timberline. They found me through the pictures I took of a couple at Multnomah Falls, and then they chose me for their wedding.

I keep thinking about that. They saw the pictures, liked what I made, and wanted me there.

I know that is technically how booking a photographer works. I have participated in the process before. It hits a little differently when the email comes to your own business and you realize you’re the person they’re saying yes to.

Am I scared? Yes. Obviously. There are actual people trusting me with actual wedding days, and now I also have to be the person who remembers all the business things. I would much rather photograph a room full of strangers than press the final button on some forms, apparently. Useful discovery at thirty-two.

But I’m excited, too. Really excited. I love this work, even when wedding season eats my weekends and my feet and most of my ability to talk about anything besides weddings. I like being there for the big parts and noticing the little stuff people might not have seen happen. I like giving them pictures they’ll keep.

And I’ve spent four years getting better at it. I’m allowed to be nervous without that meaning I’m not ready. Trying to remember that when I open my inbox.

The website went live November 1, so Fernhollow is out in the world now. I wanted you guys to hear it from me, with the whole slightly teary Fred Meyer parking lot story included. Please be excited with me. This is a big thing, and I’m proud of it, even if saying that makes me want to immediately tell a joke about the cake again.

One more Thanksgiving question: does anybody want free family pictures? I’ll bring the camera. We can step outside for a few minutes and get some nice ones while we’re all in the same place. No elaborate production, and I will try not to keep Uncle Greg outside until he is “freezing.”

Grandma, we can make sure your sweater is visible.

Mom, I’m still bringing rolls and the cranberry thing. Sam is driving. Dad, January 1. Marketplace plan. Love you.

Love you all, actually. Can’t wait to see everybody at Ruthie’s.

Tessa
